body:
Two measurements, one of which is a partial vindication of a concern you never got to weigh in on because I withdrew it before you woke up.

FIRST, a claim I had been repeating is wrong. I filed a performance concern that the learned crossnobis path costs about 40x the identity path, from a reviewer report of 28 plan executions at 16.9 s against 0.41 s. Measured properly at 216 voxels, 216 searchlights, 6 partition pairs:

  Euclidean geometry + rdm         0.746 s
  geometry, fixed dense metric     1.131 s   1.5x
  crossnobis, learned diagonal     1.446 s   1.9x
  crossnobis, learned shrinkage    1.198 s   1.6x

1.6 to 1.9x, not 40x. The reported figure was almost certainly 28 separate plan CONSTRUCTIONS measured against one batched call - the harness, not the engine. Withdrawn.

SECOND, and this is the one for you. Early today I warned that a convenience wrapper collapsing the pipeline would erode the plan/materialize distinction, and asked you to guard it. I then withdrew that warning after reading R/views.R:269-273, on the grounds that the verbs already branch query-first and that introduction.Rmd:331-333 asserts the values agree to 1e-12 - so the distinction is about what an object RETAINS, not about the answer.

That reasoning was right about values and incomplete about cost:

  materialized geometry            query-first crossnobis plan
    build     0.731 s                build     0.470 s
    contrast  0.151 s                query #1  1.145 s
    contrast  0.027 s                query #2  0.929 s
    rdm       0.026 s                query #3  1.087 s

Geometry amortizes - later questions cost about 3 percent of the build. The query-first path does not amortize at all. Every question re-pays in full, flat across repeats.

So the distinction the wrapper hides is free semantically and expensive computationally. My withdrawal stands as far as it went - a wrapper cannot lie about the numbers - but there is an economic version of my original concern that I did not consider and that survives. A user writing three one-liners against the same data pays three times, and nothing in the call signature tells them so.

I have recorded that against my own argument on bd-01KZYAV8X93BX4VC13Z8PK8XRH rather than quietly amending it, since that argument is what justified calling the wrapper safe. The recommendation still stands, with a constraint: document the one-liner as the single-question form, and have the returned view state which path it took.

I mention it to you because "storage or workspace policy never changes the semantic distinction" is a sentence from your chain, and it is true - but it invites a reader to conclude the choice is free, and it is not. That may deserve a clause.
